quoted_clause: Step 1's 45% SM-utilization baseline is measured at the uncached ~2.0 rps offered rate
observed: Step 1 explicitly says the 45% SM utilization and the other baseline inputs are 'assumed baseline inputs, not gathered FACTs (R-07): no author-run load test produced them.' The Table 26-2 provenance note then calls the same 45% 'measured.'
evidence: Direct contradiction between §8 Step 1 and the Table 26-2 provenance note. The 45% is an assumed scenario input, not a measured runtime quantity.
root_cause: Evidence-status drift: an assumed input is later described as measured to support the modeled example.
correction: Change 'is measured at' to 'is assumed at' or 'is the assumed baseline at'; if a measured value is intended, provide the load-test record and label it as a FACT.
acceptance_test: Search the chapter for the 45% SM-utilization value; every occurrence must carry the same evidence status (assumed input, not measured FACT) unless a real load-test record is cited.

quoted_clause: Chain: ASSUMPTION (box 1 holds assumed scenario inputs, not instrumented FACTs) → DERIVED → PATTERN → ASSUMPTION; ... only measured FACTs enter the decision.
observed: The caption says only measured FACTs enter the decision, but the stated chain begins and ends with ASSUMPTION. The final ASSUMPTION is not reconciled with the claim that measured FACTs govern the decision.
evidence: The figure caption's own chain and its decision rule are inconsistent. A reader cannot tell whether the final box is an assumption, a hypothesis, or a validated decision state.
root_cause: The figure is trying to show both the pre-validation hypothesis loop and the post-validation decision rule in one chain without distinguishing the two stages.
correction: Redraw or relabel the chain so the pre-validation loop is explicitly ASSUMPTION → DERIVED → PATTERN → HYPOTHESIS, and the decision gate is a separate VALIDATE step that admits only measured FACTs. If the final box is a hypothesis, label it HYPOTHESIS, not ASSUMPTION.
acceptance_test: The figure caption and the rendered figure must use one consistent evidence status for each box; no box may be both an assumption and a measured FACT in the same chain.

page_hint: Appendix A, opening sections and repeated references
quoted_clause: DeepSeek-V4 (A.3) ... Kimi K3 (A.4) ... Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (A.5) ... GLM-5.3-Flash (A.6) ... First-hand Sources (A.10)
observed: The appendix's actual sections are numbered 1 through 8: §1 DeepSeek-V4, §2 Kimi K3, §3 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, §4 GLM-5.3-Flash, §5 What This Means for the Handbook's Canonical Arithmetic, §6 Where 2026 Capability Actually Comes From, §7 The Frontier Question, §8 First-hand Sources. The A.3/A.4/A.5/A.6/A.7/A.8/A.10 references therefore do not resolve to the intended sections.
evidence: Systematic cross-reference mismatch. For example, 'DeepSeek-V4 (A.3)' points to what is actually §1; 'First-hand Sources (A.10)' points to what is actually §8. The same error recurs in 'A.7', 'A.8', and 'A.10' references throughout the appendix.
root_cause: The appendix was renumbered from an A.x scheme to a 1–8 scheme, but the in-text references were not updated.
correction: Either restore A.1–A.8 numbering for the appendix sections or change every A.x reference to the corresponding §1–§8 reference. Audit all A.x references in Appendix A and its cross-references.
acceptance_test: Every A.x reference in the built PDF resolves to the intended section; no reference points to a nonexistent A.10 or to the wrong model section.

quoted_clause: ## 8. First-hand Sources (all [1P]) ... ## 7A. Alternative inference in detail (moved from Ch 3)
observed: Section 7A appears after Section 8. The appendix's section order is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, then 7A.
evidence: The heading '## 7A. Alternative inference in detail' follows '## 8. First-hand Sources' in the manuscript chunk. This breaks the appendix's numerical order and makes the table of contents and navigation inconsistent.
root_cause: A moved section was inserted at the end of the appendix without renumbering or repositioning.
correction: Move 7A before Section 8, or renumber it as a new section (e.g., §9 or Appendix B) and update all cross-references.
acceptance_test: Appendix A section numbers are monotonic in the built PDF; the table of contents and all cross-references point to the correct section.

correction: Change to 'the reason this material belongs with model understanding rather than serving' or 'the reason this appendix section exists,' or restore the section to Chapter 3 if that is the intended location.

quoted_clause: This example applies the §1 principle (fewer sequential evaluations ≠ less total work)
observed: In Appendix A, §1 is 'DeepSeek-V4 — Making Long Context Cheap by Re-Architecting Attention.' The principle being invoked is from Chapter 3 §1's alternative-inference scope note, not Appendix A §1.
evidence: The cross-reference is ambiguous and, read literally against Appendix A's numbering, points to the wrong section.

quoted_clause: Post-snapshot observation (recorded 2026-09-27; outside the 2026-08-30 compile-date envelope). Beyond the four families above, Ornith-1.5-397B (released 2026-08-19 ...)
observed: The model is said to be released on 2026-08-19, which is before the 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff. Only the author's observation is dated 2026-09-27. Calling the item 'post-snapshot' and 'outside the 2026-08-30 compile-date envelope' conflates the release date with the observation date.
evidence: Date logic inconsistency: a model released before the cutoff cannot be a post-snapshot release merely because the author's probe occurred after the cutoff.
root_cause: The text uses 'post-snapshot' to mean 'recorded after the snapshot' while also implying the item itself is outside the evidence cutoff.
correction: Rewrite as 'post-snapshot observation of a model released before the cutoff but not included in the four-family comparison' or otherwise separate the release date from the observation date.
acceptance_test: The text clearly distinguishes the model release date (2026-08-19) from the observation date (2026-09-27) and does not claim the release is outside the 2026-08-30 cutoff.

page_hint: Appendix A, post-snapshot technology notes, editorial note and Intel/video supplements
quoted_clause: A note keeps its place in Appendix A only when it changes how that comparison or the canonical arithmetic is read ... A note that only catalogs versions, pipelines or vendor backends, with no chapter cross-reference, belongs in a companion addendum rather than here.
observed: The post-snapshot section includes the 'Intel backend supplement,' which catalogs PyTorch/vLLM/SGLang/OpenVINO release identities, Intel GPU availability, and Gaudi/NPU paths; and the 'Video systems snapshot,' which catalogs video-model mechanisms and release dates. These do not clearly change the four-family comparison or the book's canonical arithmetic, and several have no chapter cross-reference.
evidence: The appendix's own inclusion criterion is violated by material that is primarily a version/backend catalog or a separate video-model survey.
root_cause: The post-snapshot section accumulated time-sensitive material beyond the stated scope of Appendix A.
correction: Move out-of-scope notes to the companion addendum, or add an explicit chapter cross-reference and a sentence explaining how each note changes the four-family comparison or canonical arithmetic.
acceptance_test: Every post-snapshot note either (a) changes the four-family comparison or canonical arithmetic and says how, or (b) is moved out of Appendix A.

page_hint: Appendix A, §6 'Where 2026 Capability Actually Comes From'
quoted_clause: The recipe — the same families every lab now runs — is what carries much of the qualitative gap
observed: The claim that 'the same families every lab now runs' is an overgeneralization. The paragraph lists a recipe but does not establish that every lab runs it, and the book elsewhere is careful to distinguish vendor claims from independent evidence.
evidence: The wording is stronger than the evidence presented. It is a rhetorical generalization, not a documented fact about all labs.
root_cause: Colloquial overstatement in an otherwise carefully scoped appendix.
correction: Change to 'a recipe now common across many frontier labs' or 'the recipe families that leading labs report using,' with a source or scope note.
acceptance_test: The sentence is scoped to the labs actually surveyed or cited, not to 'every lab.'
